skill.name: better-accessibility
skill.description: Reviews and fixes keyboard and focus behavior, ARIA, accessible names, forms, screen-reader announcements, motion and zoom in your project against WCAG 2.2.
skill.summary: Review and fix web accessibility barriers with WCAG 2.2 criteria and explicit verification results.
skill.author: jakubkrehel

security_audit.summary: All 50 static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, CSS, HTML attributes, or accessibility review terminology. The reviewed files contain accessibility guidance, not shell execution or system reconnaissance. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, data exfiltration, or other malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Web interfaces can block users who rely on keyboards, screen readers, or zoom. This skill guides targeted fixes and reports WCAG 2.2 criteria with verification limits.
actual_capabilities: Review keyboard paths, focus indicators, modal focus restoration, and client-side navigation.
Identify missing accessible names, incorrect ARIA usage, and inappropriate HTML control semantics.
Guide form labeling, autocomplete attributes, inline validation, and accessible submission states.
Recommend live regions, image alternatives, landmarks, and skip links for screen-reader access.
Review target sizes, drag alternatives, reduced motion, timed content, zoom, and reflow.
Group accessibility findings by principle and severity, with locations, fixes, user impact, and verification status.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and examples, not a bundled browser or automated testing engine.
Browser and screen-reader behavior needs manual verification with available tools and target platform combinations.
Contrast measurement, color changes, typography, layout, and wording are delegated to related skills.
A scoped review does not establish full WCAG conformance or legal compliance.

use_cases.title: Fix Keyboard Barriers in Components
use_cases.description: Review dialogs, tabs, and navigation for keyboard paths, visible focus, and focus restoration before release.

use_cases.title: Verify Accessible User Flows
use_cases.description: Check form submission, error announcements, and status updates through keyboard and screen-reader workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Shared Interface Patterns
use_cases.description: Assess shared controls for names, roles, states, target sizes, and reduced-motion behavior across a component library.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Single Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component] for accessible names, native semantics, and visible focus. Explain each barrier and recommend the smallest fix.

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Accessible Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Review and fix [form] labels, autocomplete, validation, and pending submission behavior. Preserve project conventions and report checks you cannot verify.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Interactive Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [flow] for keyboard navigation, modal focus, live announcements, and zoom. Cite applicable WCAG 2.2 criteria and separate observed failures from unverified checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Shared Component Library
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [component library] for systemic accessibility barriers. Fix shared root causes, group findings by principle and severity, and list all affected locations.

output_examples.input: Review an icon-only delete control that has no accessible name.
output: High severity: The delete control has no accessible name, so screen-reader users cannot identify its action.
WCAG 4.1.2: Give the control a descriptive accessible name and hide its decorative icon from assistive technology.
Verification: Source review identifies the missing name. Browser accessibility-tree inspection and screen-reader testing are not verified.

output_examples.input: Review a form that shows errors through red borders alone.
output: The form communicates validation errors only through color, creating a barrier for users who cannot distinguish the border state.
WCAG 1.4.1 and 3.3.1: Add inline error text, associate it with each failing field, and focus the first invalid field after submission.
Verification: Confirm that errors are announced with their fields. Target browser and screen-reader behavior is not verified without testing.

output_examples.input: Review a success toast whose polite announcement region appears with its message.
output: The newly mounted polite region may not announce the success message consistently.
Keep an empty status region mounted before updates, then change its text when the operation completes.
Verification: Test repeated announcements with the target screen readers. Leave keyboard focus on the current control.

best_practices: Provide the component scope and affected user flow, then request findings tied to WCAG criteria or concrete task barriers.
Preserve native HTML behavior and project styling conventions when applying accessibility fixes.
Combine source review with keyboard and screen-reader testing, and clearly mark checks that remain unverified.
anti_patterns: Treating a source-only review or automated audit as proof of complete accessibility conformance.
Adding ARIA roles to generic elements instead of using suitable native controls.
Removing focus indicators, blocking paste, or preventing zoom to preserve a visual design.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available project access and testing tools depend on your environment.

faq.question: Which accessibility standard does it use?
faq.answer: It uses WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA criteria. It distinguishes recommendations and AAA targets from required thresholds.

faq.question: Can it fix project code?
faq.answer: The instructions guide code fixes using existing project conventions. Applying changes requires an AI environment with access to the relevant files.

faq.question: Does it include automated accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No testing engine is bundled. The guidance calls for automated audits when browser tools are available and marks unavailable checks as unverified.

faq.question: Does it measure color contrast?
faq.answer: It identifies applicable contrast requirements but delegates rendered contrast measurement to better-colors. Color changes require a request.

faq.question: Does a successful review guarantee compliance?
faq.answer: No. Results cover inspected components and completed checks only. Full conformance requires broader assessment, including manual testing with assistive technology.
